soru: What are the most important works and open problems in learning robotic manipulation from human video demonstrations?

alt_sorular.soru: What are the foundations and classic methods for learning manipulation from human demonstrations and video (imitation learning, learning from observation, third-person imitation)?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when seminal LfD/LfO works (e.g., BCO, time-contrastive networks, third-person imitation, imitation from observation) and early video-to-robot pipelines are identified.

alt_sorular.soru: How are visual representations pretrained on human video (egocentric, internet-scale) and reused for robot manipulation?
sorgular: "visual representation" human video robot manipulation pretraining
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when key pretrained representations (R3M, MVP, VIP, Voltron, VC-1, LIV) and their evaluations are covered.

alt_sorular.soru: What methods extract actionable intermediate representations (affordances, hand poses, object/point tracks, optical flow) from human videos for transfer to robots?
sorgular: hand-object interaction human video robot transfer
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when affordance-based (VRB), track/flow-based (ATM, Track2Act, Im2Flow2Act, General Flow), and hand-pose retargeting approaches (DexMV, VideoDex) are captured.

alt_sorular.soru: How do video prediction / world models and latent action models trained on human video enable robot policies (video generation as policy, latent actions, VLA pretraining on human videos)?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when UniPi, latent action pretraining (LAPA, Genie), video-language planning, and recent VLA works using human video (e.g., GR-1/GR-2, EgoVLA) are covered.

alt_sorular.soru: Which datasets and data-collection systems of human manipulation video are used (egocentric datasets, handheld grippers, wearable capture)?
sorgular: egocentric dexterous manipulation dataset hand pose
human demonstration data collection wearable robot learning
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when major video datasets (Ego4D, EPIC-KITCHENS, Something-Something, HOI4D, EgoDex) and in-the-wild collection systems (UMI, DexCap) are identified.

alt_sorular.soru: How are rewards and task specifications learned from human videos for reinforcement learning on robots?
sorgular: reward learning from human videos robot
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when reward-from-video works (DVD, XIRL, Concept2Robot, VIP/LIV rewards) and their limitations are covered.

alt_sorular.soru: How are these methods evaluated and what open problems remain (embodiment gap, scaling, generalization, dexterity, benchmarks)?
sorgular: learning from human videos survey robotics
scaling robot learning human video challenges
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when surveys, benchmark/evaluation protocols, and clearly stated open challenges (embodiment mismatch, missing actions, evaluation standards) are collected.

calismalar.baslik: Imitation from Observation: Learning to Imitate Behaviors from Raw Video via Context Translation
calismalar.gerekce: Foundational imitation-from-observation work learning to imitate behaviors from raw video via context translation.
calismalar.alinti: we observe another person performing some behavior and then figure out which actions will realize that behavior

calismalar.baslik: Behavioral Cloning from Observation
calismalar.gerekce: Highly cited behavioral cloning from observation, addressing learning from observation only with self-supervised pre-experience.
calismalar.alinti: there are two particular aspects that have largely been overlooked: (1) that the learning is done from observation only

calismalar.baslik: Time-Contrastive Networks: Self-Supervised Learning from Video
calismalar.gerekce: Classic self-supervised representation learning from multi-view video using a metric learning loss for imitation.
calismalar.alinti: We train our representations using a metric learning loss, where multiple simultaneous viewpoints of the same observation are attracted in the embedding space

calismalar.baslik: R3M: A Universal Visual Representation for Robot Manipulation
calismalar.gerekce: R3M shows visual representations pretrained on diverse human video enable data-efficient downstream robot manipulation learning.
calismalar.alinti: We study how visual representations pre-trained on diverse human video data can enable data-efficient learning of downstream robotic manipulation tasks

calismalar.baslik: Ego4D: Around the World in 3,000 Hours of Egocentric Video
calismalar.gerekce: Ego4D provides 3,670 hours of daily-life egocentric video, a foundational dataset for human-video robot learning.
calismalar.alinti: It offers 3,670 hours of daily-life activity video spanning hundreds of scenarios (household, outdoor, workplace, leisure, etc.)

calismalar.baslik: VIP: Towards Universal Visual Reward and Representation via Value-Implicit Pre-Training
calismalar.gerekce: VIP learns a universal visual reward and representation from large, diverse offline human videos via value-implicit pre-training.
calismalar.alinti: learning from large, diverse, offline human videos has emerged as a promising path towards acquiring a generally useful visual representation for control

calismalar.baslik: Real-World Robot Learning with Masked Visual Pre-training
calismalar.gerekce: Scales masked visual pretraining to 4.5M Internet and egocentric images, training a 307M-parameter vision transformer for real-world robots.
calismalar.alinti: Finally, we train a 307M parameter vision transformer on a massive collection of 4.5M images from the Internet and egocentric videos

calismalar.baslik: Affordances from Human Videos as a Versatile Representation for Robotics
calismalar.gerekce: Trains visual affordance models from human videos estimating where and how humans interact, a versatile robotics representation.
calismalar.alinti: we train a visual affordance model that estimates where and how in the scene a human is likely to interact

calismalar.baslik: Universal Manipulation Interface: In-The-Wild Robot Teaching Without In-The-Wild Robots
calismalar.gerekce: UMI uses hand-held grippers for portable, low-cost, information-rich in-the-wild data collection without in-the-wild robots.
calismalar.alinti: UMI employs hand-held grippers coupled with careful interface design to enable portable, low-cost, and information-rich data collection

calismalar.baslik: Latent Action Pretraining from Videos
calismalar.gerekce: Latent action pretraining learns discrete latent actions between frames with a VQ-VAE objective from unlabeled videos.
calismalar.alinti: We first train an action quantization model leveraging VQ-VAE-based objective to learn discrete latent actions between image frames

calismalar.baslik: Learning Generalizable Robotic Reward Functions from "In-The-Wild" Human Videos
calismalar.gerekce: Learns generalizable robotic reward functions from in-the-wild human videos such as YouTube.
calismalar.alinti: videos of humans (e.g. YouTube) contain an extensive collection of people doing interesting tasks

calismalar.baslik: DexMV: Imitation Learning for Dexterous Manipulation from Human Videos
calismalar.gerekce: DexMV extracts 3D hand and object poses from videos and translates human motion into robot demonstrations for dexterity.
calismalar.alinti: we extract 3D hand and object poses from videos, and propose a novel demonstration translation method to convert human motion to robot demonstrations

calismalar.baslik: Track2Act: Predicting Point Tracks from Internet Videos enables Generalizable Robot Manipulation
calismalar.gerekce: Track2Act predicts point tracks trained on diverse web videos of humans and robots for generalizable manipulation.
calismalar.alinti: can be trained with diverse videos on the web including those of humans and robots manipulating everyday objects

calismalar.baslik: Robot Learning from Human Videos: A Survey
calismalar.gerekce: Recent survey of robot learning from human videos, reviewing policy foundations and interfaces for incorporating human videos.
calismalar.alinti: We first review the policy learning foundations in robotics, and then describe the fundamental interfaces to incorporate human videos.

calismalar.baslik: EgoDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Large-Scale Egocentric Video
calismalar.gerekce: EgoDex offers 829 hours of egocentric video paired with 3D hand and finger tracking for dexterous manipulation.
calismalar.alinti: EgoDex has 829 hours of egocentric video with paired 3D hand and finger tracking data collected at the time of recording

calismalar.baslik: MimicPlay: Long-Horizon Imitation Learning by Watching Human Play
calismalar.gerekce: MimicPlay uses human play data for long-horizon imitation learning, exploiting rich physical interaction information.
calismalar.alinti: we hypothesize that human play data contain rich and salient information about physical interactions that can readily facilitate robot policy learning

calismalar.baslik: XIRL: Cross-embodiment Inverse Reinforcement Learning
calismalar.gerekce: XIRL learns cross-embodiment rewards so agents learn policies from videos of other agents such as humans.
calismalar.alinti: agents learn policies from videos of other agents (such as humans) demonstrating the same task

calismalar.baslik: Any-point Trajectory Modeling for Policy Learning
calismalar.gerekce: Any-point trajectory modeling provides control guidance from video, enabling robust policies with minimal action-labeled data.
calismalar.alinti: Once trained, these trajectories provide detailed control guidance, enabling the learning of robust visuomotor policies with minimal action-labeled data

calismalar.baslik: VideoDex: Learning Dexterity from Internet Videos
calismalar.gerekce: VideoDex leverages visual, action, and physical priors from internet human video datasets to guide robot dexterity.
calismalar.alinti: We build a learning algorithm, VideoDex, that leverages visual, action, and physical priors from human video datasets to guide robot behavior

calismalar.baslik: DexCap: Scalable and Portable Mocap Data Collection System for Dexterous Manipulation
calismalar.gerekce: DexCap provides portable, occlusion-resistant wrist and finger motion capture for scalable dexterous data collection.
calismalar.alinti: DexCap offers precise, occlusion-resistant tracking of wrist and finger motions based on SLAM and electromagnetic field together with 3D observations

calismalar.baslik: Gen2Act: Human Video Generation in Novel Scenarios enables Generalizable Robot Manipulation
calismalar.gerekce: Gen2Act uses video generation models trained on web data to generate human videos that enable generalizable manipulation.
calismalar.alinti: Instead of attempting to scale robot data collection which is expensive, we show how we can leverage video generation models trained on easily available web data, for enabling generalization.

calismalar.gerekce: Learns task-agnostic reward functions for robotic manipulation from unlabeled videos of humans solving diverse tasks.
calismalar.alinti: we use unlabeled videos of humans solving a wide range of manipulation tasks to learn a task-agnostic reward function for robotic manipulation policies

calismalar.baslik: Robotic Offline RL from Internet Videos via Value-Function Pre-Training
calismalar.gerekce: Shows value learning on video datasets yields representations more conducive to downstream robotic offline RL.
calismalar.alinti: We show that value learning on video datasets learns representations that are more conducive to downstream robotic offline RL

calismalar.gerekce: AVID uses CycleGAN pixel-level translation to convert human demonstrations into robot videos for multi-stage tasks.
calismalar.alinti: We instead take an automated approach and perform pixel-level image translation via CycleGAN to convert the human demonstration into a video of a robot

calismalar.baslik: What Matters When Cotraining Robot Manipulation Policies on Everyday Human Videos?
calismalar.gerekce: Analyzes cotraining on everyday human video, finding hand pose quality and inherent motion gap limit transfer.
calismalar.alinti: We find that hand pose quality affects transfer, but even with accurate hands, the inherent motion gap hinders transfer

calismalar.baslik: H2RBench: A Real-to-Sim Benchmark for Evaluating Human-to-Robot Transfer

calismalar.gerekce: DexUMI uses the human hand as the interface to transfer dexterous manipulation skills to various robot hands.
